statement: For every finite simple graph G on at most ten vertices that is 3-degenerate (degeneracy at most 3), has maximum degree at most 4, and contains no K_{3,4} subgraph, q_B(G) is at most 9. This bound is sharp because q_B(K_{3,3})=9. Consequently, any legal graph with q_B(G)=10 must have a connected component on at least eleven vertices. This is an exact exhaustive computational result and does not determine M_3(4).
contribution: A reproducible exact enumeration and dual-solver verification excludes every value-10 witness through order ten, improving the smallest possible order of a witness to at least eleven. Connected legal classes are exhaustively generated by non-cut-vertex deletion and exact isomorphism deduplication; checked Glucose4 colorings and a separate exact DSATUR backtracker agree for all classes. The original 9-versus-10 problem remains unresolved.
